reviewer: Claude (Opus 5) review agent, independent of the extractor; no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the 490 records of the Bacformer and BacBench batch (13 sources, 12 models, 26 configurations, 1 benchmark, 6 tasks, 17 protocols, 6 datasets, 2 dataset subsets, 186 evaluations, 186 results, 35 claims) by an agent that did not extract it, against the extraction frozen at batch.jsonl SHA-256 776ec11726d7f9f42ec845745341abe0bbfb3006c74b9851e00ca8910995a1ac. No vocabulary concept was missing and data/vocab is untouched. The eleven non-PDF artifacts were downloaded again at review time: every one hashed to exactly the value its source record records and is byte-identical to the copy in artifacts/. The two bioRxiv PDFs could not be hash-matched and were not expected to be: bioRxiv regenerates the file on request, so two fresh downloads of version 3 gave 0287e3b6c1272cbe9f02a36b3b2abd0d26fddf3f214ad11aff9107298494cc70 and 47fc16b387904db0a4ad935d3fd8e2cc375af497fac4dd899c833468fd267382, both different from the recorded hash and from the two the extractor saw, while the pdftotext -layout text layer of both reproduced 86636e89b167d7304b3a83ee7f159cad0a9bdbe97019588ce836087b8fe3b0b2 byte for byte, which is what the archived artifacts/biorxiv-665723v3-text-layer.txt.gz decompresses to and what every stored value was read from. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly against a text layer regenerated from a fresh download: 36 in_cell, 150 in_row, nothing else, and its value-check.tsv was byte-identical to the extractor's. All 186 cells were then re-read by review/recheck_cells.py, written for this pass, which uses neither extractor script and does not read the text layer they read: it takes word bounding boxes from pdftotext -bbox-layout, groups words into printed lines by y coordinate, derives each table's column boundaries from the x extent of that table's own printed header words, and assigns every number to a column by where it sits on the page. It asserts the printed row order, that every column of every row is filled, that each cell holds exactly a mean and a spread with its own plus-minus sign, and for Tables S13 and S18 that each group header sits geometrically over the two columns named after it. Every printed value, mean, spread, spread string and spread source column matched, with no disagreement, and the six tables print no cell the batch leaves unrecorded. Three negative controls (two cells of one row exchanged, one cell taking its neighbour's value, every Table S18 locator moved one column to the right) were all rejected and the unmutated batch accepted; review/negative-controls.txt holds the log. A manual sample of 47 cells was read by eye against the printed table bodies: 24 drawn over all 186 with random.sample at seed 20261115, all 18 cells of Table S12, and the eight Evo and Evo-2 cells of Tables S1 and S14 where the printed row order differs from the other tables; all matched, column assignment included. Every missing_metadata entry, null and uncertainty denominator was checked against the source, and the access states were rechecked at review time rather than taken from notes.md: at 2026-11-15T23:41:36Z the two README-listed checkpoints bacformer-causal-protein-family-modeling-complete-genomes and bacformer-for-essential-genes-prediction returned HTTP 401 from both the web page and the model API, and bacformer-for-ppi-prediction returned 200. Two corrections were applied before the batch was stored, both recorded in docs/reviews/2026-11-15-bacformer.md.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude (Opus 5) agent, independent of the extractor but not human scientific review. Transcription was checked against the pinned sources; nothing was reproduced and no value was recomputed.

Correction applied: the 168 results printed on a 0 to 100 scale carried unit percent. data/vocab/unit.ttl says in the scope note of unitless that a unitless statistic printed x100 stays unitless with unit_detail 'printed x100', because percent would imply a proportion, and the store holds 4403 AUROC results as unitless against 9 as percent. The unit concept and its detail were changed on those 168 results and on their uncertainty objects. No printed value, numeric value or spread was altered.

Correction applied in a second pass, after the batch was stored: the 14 protocols governing those results carried unit percent as well, which would have left a protocol declaring one unit over results declaring another. review/fix_protocol_units.py applied the same change in data/entities/protocols.jsonl and in batch.jsonl together, and it was recorded with npm run records -- change against this review. The three strain-clustering protocols are printed on a 0 to 1 scale and were already unitless.

Correction applied: the claim bacformer-20261115-claim-preprint-version-differences, the version 2 source description and a version 3 source limitation all stated that version 2 prints different values for the same analyses. Both figures cited as examples are identical in the two versions, read from 200 dpi renders of version 2 pages 5 and 8, which print 'almost 95% balanced accuracy across diverse genera' and '0.81 +/- 0.07 median AUROC across diverse genomes'. The assertion was replaced by what the sources support, and the limitation now records that no systematic numeric comparison of the two versions was made.

The version 3 PDF's artifact_sha256 is one download's hash and no refetch will reproduce it, because bioRxiv regenerates the container on request. The hash was not changed. The source record now carries review_artifact and review_artifact_matches_original_artifact_sha256 false, and its limitations name the text layer as the stable identity.

The version 2 PDF is unverifiable at any layer. Its container hash did not reproduce (refetch af77c2be437b151b5e464f2f5078f6b97b95a29c2913affefc566337eecfbad4) and the record pins nothing below the container; its text layer mis-encodes digits, which this review confirmed against page renders. No value or figure in the batch rests on it.

The parameter-count disagreement is unresolved and stays so: nine claims hold each printed figure with its own locator and no model record carries a parameter value, which the attribute registry makes unavoidable since the model kind declares no such field. No printed figure was marked as an error and no evidence concern was raised over the BacBench README's 27M for Bacformer Large.

Table S16's caption says the spread is across 5 seeds while the Methods say three independent runs with different data splits. The conflict stays a claim plus a result-level warning on the 24 results, and the uncertainty asserts no replicate count. No evidence concern: the conflict is about what the spread covers, not about the means.

The Table S12 checkpoint stays unassigned. Preprint Methods paragraph 331 says all checkpoints are those of Table S9, which names the complete-genome checkpoints, while the BacBench README's footnote on those two rows says historical strain clustering runs used the MAG checkpoints because the inputs are MAGs, and the data are 6,071 MAGs. The two clustering configurations keep missing_metadata.checkpoint conflicting and point at the family record.

The strain clustering protocols keep the Leiden selection as a limitation and a claim, with no evidence concern: the hyperparameters were chosen on the reported metrics for all six systems alike, so the bias is a property of the protocol rather than a defect that should withhold the table.

No figure was read, no main-text prose figure was extracted and Tables S2, S10, S11, S15 and S17 were not extracted. The review did not widen the scope; Table S15 stays out because BacBench does not list protein function prediction among its tasks.
No split manifest, seed list or BacBench commit is published for any run, so none of these numbers is reproducible as printed, and no evaluation is marked reproduced.
The benchmark is author-built: the same group built Bacformer, built BacBench, curated every dataset and ran all twelve systems. The claim recording that was checked and kept.
No discrepancy involves this batch. None of its record IDs was in the store before this review, so no discrepancies.json could list them; the knowledge-graph build after the add may raise new leads.
source_artifacts below is written from the source records by npm run batch -- hash and therefore lists the two PDF hashes as recorded. Only the eleven non-PDF artifacts were verified against it.
